definition: A specific, identifiable subnetwork of neurons and connections within a model hypothesized to implement a particular, interpretable computational function.
details: The concept of circuits is central to mechanistic interpretability research, which aims to identify and understand these functional subnetworks much as one might analyze a circuit diagram in traditional engineering.

explainer.lead: A circuit is a proposed small team of neurons and connections inside a model that performs one understandable job. Finding such teams could turn an opaque model into something researchers can explain and test piece by piece.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a huge machine with thousands of tiny parts, but only a few parts work together to ring a bell. A circuit is like that little group: researchers think it has one job inside the much bigger machine. They test the idea by watching the group and changing what it does.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers start with a specific model behavior, trace candidate neurons and connections, and use interventions on those candidates to test whether they support the proposed function. The main pitfall is treating activation or correlation as proof: a circuit remains a hypothesis until the evidence supports its claimed role.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a model M, a circuit C = (V_C, E_C) is an identifiable subnetwork of neurons V_C and connections E_C hypothesized to implement an interpretable function f. Circuit analysis relates this subnetwork to a specified model behavior, but identifying relevant components does not by itself establish a complete explanation.

explainer.example: Suppose a small language model often predicts ")" after seeing "(". Researchers find neurons that respond to "(" and connections that later strengthen the prediction of ")"; testing whether changing this subnetwork changes that prediction evaluates the hypothesis of a parenthesis-closing circuit.

usedIn.name: Mechanistic interpretability
usedIn.detail: Researchers use circuits to break model behavior into functional subnetworks that can be examined individually.

usedIn.name: Neural network analysis
usedIn.detail: The circuit viewpoint connects particular neurons and connections with an interpretable computational role.

explainer.intuition: A large neural network may contain smaller, recognizable mechanisms, much as a complicated device contains circuits with distinct purposes. A circuit names one proposed mechanism rather than treating the whole model as a single unexplained unit.
howItWorks: Choose a specific model behavior to explain.
Identify candidate neurons involved in that behavior.
Trace connections that could combine their activity into a function.
Test the proposed circuit and refine the hypothesis.
explainer.whyItMatters: Circuits give mechanistic interpretability a concrete unit of analysis, allowing broad model behavior to be studied as testable claims about smaller components. This is analogous to understanding a device by examining its circuit diagram instead of only observing its inputs and outputs.
misconceptions: A circuit is a model subnetwork, not physical wiring.
A proposed circuit is a hypothesis, not automatically a proven explanation.
Neurons active during a behavior are not necessarily all part of its circuit.
